item.title: Pixar's New Movie Gatto Gets First In-Depth Look in Official Trailer
item.description: The first teaser for Gatto , Pixar's upcoming animated film, was released on Jun. 11, following a description of the movie's general plot and some cast members. Fans learned that Gatto is set in the Italian city of Venice, and it follows the adventures of a feral black cat named Nero, who's spent most of his nine lives recklessly working for mobster cat Rocco.

item.title: Leaked Dune Magic Secret Lair Has Amazing Value Reprints and 9 New Cards
item.description: One popular sci-fi property is the talk of the Magic: The Gathering community right now, and it's not Star Trek . On Nov. 12, leaks started to emerge online about a Dune Secret Lair drop, and while still unconfirmed, this new Universes Beyond collaboration seems legitimate.

item.title: 6 Nintendo Switch Special Editions With the Best Designs, Ranked
item.description: When a new console arrives, a lot of us rush out to buy one the minute we can afford to. At launch, there’s typically just one option, or sometimes a handful of choices with varying specifications. Personality isn’t a draw yet, beyond whatever’s standard. Over time, however, that inevitably changes.

item.title: 5 Sci-Fi Book Trilogies Where Every Entry Is Perfect
item.description: Of course, not all sci-fi trilogies are created equal. Plenty start strong only to flame out in book two or three, while others admittedly take a while to get good. But there are plenty of perfect trilogies, too. Polygon has rounded up five sci-fi book trilogies that are worth your time from start to finish. Check out the list below.

item.title: Tim Burton's Forgotten Dark Fantasy Magnum Opus Is Officially Free on Youtube
item.description: When it comes to beautiful, high-quality stop-motion animation, Laika is likely the first name that comes to mind. The studio’s hand-crafted puppetry and 3D-printing technology have brought beautiful tales to life for years, from Coraline to Kubo and the Two Strings . Each has leaned toward more adult themes with gothic narrative undertones, while still focusing heavily on family dynamics. The same is true of Laika’s most recent outing, Travis Knight’s ethereal fantasy epic, Wildwood .

item.title: Netflix's Disappointing New Western Thriller Wastes Its Brilliant Concept
item.description: Written and directed by Shana Feste, the Netflix-original film feels as if the director of Country Strong watched a couple of episodes of Yellowstone and decided to take a stab at a western-noir, centering her story on a jaded country star. The result is a missing-person mystery with three musical numbers woven into it. Heartland might be the first western-noir-musical ever made, and I wish Feste took advantage of how weird that is. Instead, it’s pure straight-to-Netflix fodder.

item.title: 26 Years Later, Charles Schulz' Final Comic Strip Is Still an All-Time Peanuts Classic
item.description: While that was the first official Peanuts comic, a similar version by Charles Schulz predated Peanuts and ran in Minnesota’s St. Paul Pioneer Press. It was called Li’l Folks and also starred cute little children, although it did not have a regular cast like Peanuts would. Li’l Folks ran from 1947 until 1950, when Schulz quit after his editor refused to give him a raise from the $10 per comic he was making. After that, Schulz brought Li’l Folks to United Feature Syndicate. The national cartoon syndicator liked the comic, but needed to change its name because of a 1930s comic strip called Little Folks . The name Peanuts was chosen because The Howdy Doody Show was popular at the time and the studio audience of children on the show was called the “Peanut gallery.” Thus, Peanuts became the name.

item.title: 5 Funniest 'Peanuts' Comics About Food Only Charles Schulz Could Come Up With
item.description: There aren't quite as many Peanuts comic strips focused on food as one might expect. Little kids do tend to live their lives in the windows between meals and snacks, and Snoopy is as obsessed with his suppertime as any other dog, but food humor was a relatively low priority in Charles Schulz's punchline rotation. Compared to baseball, philosophy, Snoopy's alternate personas, or Charlie Brown's truly existential levels of depression , food as a topic in Peanuts was kept on a low boil.

item.title: 8 Near-Perfect Xbox 360 Games That Are Forgotten Masterpieces
item.description: The Xbox 360 era was a marvelous generation and the last time publishers regularly bet on strange, original ideas. Plenty of those bets paid off, from Gears of War to Assassin's Creed . But time hasn't been kind to all of them, and some of the generation's best games have been out of the conversation so long that a whole new wave of players has never heard of them.

item.title: 44 Years Later, Star Trek’s Best Quote About Grief Is Still a Near-Perfect Sci-Fi Moment
item.description: Franchises often help us understand the pain of loss. Shows like WandaVision have been praised for their exploration of grief and the anguish that exists there. But other franchises have also explored the feelings that surround death and grief. One of the biggest science fiction franchises of all time is known for quite a few poignant moments exploring what death can bring to those who are left behind. That franchise is Star Trek and trying to figure out the best approach to loss is hard because each of the franchise's iconic series has had moments that are worth talking about.
